---
title: Native-only Web staging
description: Publish the isolated Web Worker and return an explicit 404 for unmigrated paths.
---

The owner-provisioned Web staging host is native-only. Paths admitted by the
native legal and security flags render through Start; the probe stays native.
All other paths, including login, APIs, assets and disabled native routes,
return HTTP 404 with a static **Not migrated yet** page and
`x-tuturuuu-native: not-migrated`. The page supports light and dark themes,
uses no external assets, disallows indexing and is never cached.

This decision applies only to staging. Production Web retains its existing
Next deployment and routing. Staging has no Vercel deployment, Next fallback
origin or container. The Worker verifies Access before serving native content
or the 404; local OPTIONS handling retains the existing staging CORS policy.
A static 404 needs no upstream Supabase attestation. The staging public build
identity, cookie isolation, request sanitizers and client-IP trust are retained.

Dispatch `wave1-web-staging.yaml` from main with a full admitted source SHA.
Admission requires green candidate qualification and an exact
`WAVE1_STAGING_PUBLICATION_ADMISSION` record. The record uses the shared staging
schema with `app: web`, exact `sourceSha` and `artifactSha256`; there is no
`nextDeploymentId` field. Seal the candidate, restore and accept the same emitted
bytes, then publish. If sealing produces a new digest, the release owner admits
that exact digest and reruns. No provider credential enters the build steps.

The publisher retains stop fences, exact artifact admission, protected publishing
environment, Access ingress preflight, attempt ledger, bounded upload and
post-publication readback. It never creates domains, changes Access or DNS, or
sets serving intent. A failed ingress check rolls back only the staging Worker.
Native route flags default off; enabling them is a separate release decision.

Regression coverage lives in `scripts/ci/wave1-web-staging-workflow.test.js`,
`wave1-web-publication.test.js`, `wave1-web-seal.test.mjs`, and the
`apps/web/cloudflare` handler, native document and emitted runtime tests.
